entry.literal: contempt; to the breach / birth-opening; the lads of the king of Assyria; the sons of Eden who (were) in Telassar; of the city (of) Sepharvaim; the documents … and he read it … and he spread it; the one sitting (on/above) the cherubim; your eye(s); which/who he sent; all the lands and their land; that you (are) YHWH, you alone; (as to) what you prayed to me against/concerning Sennacherib; behind you she shook (her) head; and against whom have you raised (your) voice; the far reaches of Lebanon; its junipers/cypresses; the height of its end; the forest of its orchard-land; water; the Nile-channels of Egypt; to make crash (into) ruined heaps; they were shattered and ashamed; and a field before standing grain; your ease / complacency; my hook; my bridle; the escaped of the house of Judah; and I will shield; and they rose early in the morning; dead corpses; Nisroch; Adrammelech; Sharezer; Esar-haddon
entry.standardEnglish: ASV: 'contumely', 'the children are come to the birth', 'the servants of the king of Assyria', 'the children of Eden that were in Telassar', 'the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah', 'the letter … read it … spread it', 'that sittest [above] the cherubim', 'open thine eyes', 'who hath sent to defy', 'all the countries, and their land', 'that thou art Jehovah, even thou only', 'Whereas thou hast prayed to me against Sennacherib', 'hath shaken her head at thee', 'against whom hast thou exalted thy voice and lifted up thine eyes on high? [even] against the Holy One of Israel', 'the innermost parts of Lebanon', 'the choice fir-trees thereof', 'its farthest height, the forest of its fruitful field', 'I have digged and drunk water … all the rivers of Egypt', 'to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps', 'dismayed and confounded', 'as a field [of grain] before it is grown up', 'thine arrogancy', 'my hook … my bridle', 'the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah', 'I will defend this city', 'when men arose early in the morning … dead bodies', 'Nisroch … Adrammelech and Sharezer … Esar-haddon'. JPS 1917: 'who was over the household', 'contumely', 'that sittest upon the cherubim', 'open Thine eyes', 'the cypress-trees', 'fashioned it', 'thine uproar', 'when men arose', 'Sarezer', 'Esarhaddon'. NJPS: 'who was in charge of the palace', 'Shebna, the scribe', 'disgrace', 'The babes have reached the birthstool', 'the minions of the king of Assyria', 'the Bethedenites in Telassar', 'the kings of Lair, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah', 'enthroned on the Cherubim', 'open Your eye', 'all the nations and their lands' (note: 'So 2 Kings 19.17, and 13 mss. here'), 'alone [are God]' (note: 'Supplied from 2 Kings 19.19'), 'to whom you have prayed, concerning King Sennacherib', 'shakes Her head at you', 'the remotest parts of the Lebanon', 'Its choicest cypresses', 'Its densest forest' (note: 'Lit. "Its farmland forest"'), 'drawn' (note: 'Or "dug"'), 'All the streams of Egypt', 'I designed it long ago', 'Dismayed and shamed', 'Grass of the roofs that is blasted Before the east wind' (note: 'So ms. 1QIsa; cf. 2 Kings 19.26'), 'your tumult', 'My bit', 'I will protect and save this city', '[That night] an angel of the LORD … the following morning they were all dead corpses' (ASV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS (Tanakh: The Holy Scriptures, published by JPS, 1985; not the Gender-Sensitive Edition) via Sefaria API v3; MT of Isa 37 and 2 Kgs 19 (Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra) via Sefaria API v3; all checked 2026-11-27).
entry.wohChoice: 37:3 nᵉʾāṣāh 'contempt' (modern for ASV 'contumely'); 'the children have come to the birth' (ASV image; NJPS 'birthstool' in commentary). 37:6 naʿărê 'the servants' (ASV, JPS 1917; the naʿar/ʿeḇeḏ distinction and NJPS 'minions' in commentary). 37:12 bᵉnê-ʿeḏen 'the children of Eden' (ASV, JPS 1917): the Aramean state (Amos 1:5 bêṯ ʿeḏen), not the garden; identification in commentary only. 37:13 lāʿîr 'of the city' (ASV; NJPS place name 'Lair' in commentary). 37:14 hassᵉp̄ārîm 'the letter' (singular suffixes in Isaiah; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS); 39:1 'letters'. 37:16 yōšēḇ hakkᵉrūḇîm 'who is enthroned on the cherubim', the fixed title in the corpus wording of 2 Sam 6:2 (2-samuel-woh, stable; NJPS 'enthroned on'; JPS 1917 'sittest upon'), replacing the draft's 'who sits enthroned above the cherubim' (ASV's supplied '[above]'). 37:17 ʿênᵉḵā 'your eyes' (defective plural, ASV, JPS 1917; NJPS singular in commentary). 37:18 MT kol-hāʾărāṣôṯ 'all the lands and their land' (2 Kgs 19:17 haggôyim in commentary). 37:20 MT 'that you are YHWH, you alone' (Kings ʾĕlōhîm in commentary). 37:21 ʾel 'against' (ASV, JPS 1917). 37:22 perfects as present perfects; 'has shaken her head at you' (ASV; literal 'behind you' in commentary). 37:23 ASV/NJPS construal, one question answered by 'Against the Holy One of Israel!'. 37:24 yarkᵉṯê lᵉḇānôn 'the far reaches of Lebanon' (concordant with 14:13, 15 'the far reaches'; replaces the draft's ASV 'the innermost parts'); bᵉrōšāyw 'its choice cypresses' (14:8; 41:19); mᵉrôm qiṣṣô 'its farthest height' (ASV); yaʿar karmillô 'the forest of its fruitful field' (common noun, as 10:18; 29:17; 32:15; against the place name of 35:2); tenses with ASV. 37:25 MT māyim 'water' (Kings zārîm in commentary); yᵉʾōrê māṣôr 'all the rivers of Egypt' (central yeor Isaiah clause). 37:26 ASV construal 'to lay waste fortified cities into ruinous heaps'. 37:27 ḥattû wāḇōšû 'dismayed and ashamed' (as 20:5); MT šᵉḏēmāh 'as a field of grain before it is grown up' (ASV; Kings/1QIsaᵃ 'blasted' in commentary). 37:29 šaʾănankā 'your arrogance' (ASV): the complacency sense of šaʾănān (Amos 6:1; Ps 123:4), kept apart from 'quiet' at 32:18 and 33:20 (lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33); ḥaḥî 'my hook', mitgî 'my bridle'. 37:31 pᵉlêṭaṯ 'the survivors' (as 4:2; 10:20). 37:35 gnn 'protect' (as 31:5). 37:36 wayyaškîmû ḇabbōqer 'when people arose early in the morning' (ASV, JPS 1917 supply 'men'; gender-neutral supplied subject so the clause cannot be read of the dead; replaces the draft's 'when they arose'); pᵉḡārîm mēṯîm 'dead bodies' (ASV); malʾaḵ YHWH 'the messenger of YHWH' under central malakh-yhwh-messenger (the decision left open by lexical-cruxes-isaiah-33 is recorded here). 37:38 ASV name forms 'Nisroch', 'Adrammelech', 'Sharezer', 'Esar-haddon'; ʾereṣ ʾărārāṭ 'the land of Ararat' (central harei-ararat not applied).
entry.rationale: Each item is a site where the line translates the Masoretic text of Isaiah and chooses among the renderings of the standard versions; none carries a project reading, and the parallel text of 2 Kgs 19 is reported in commentary, never adopted (wave I-6 ruling 3). (1) Three line changes are made. At 37:16 the participle yōšēḇ has no preposition, so every version supplies one: ASV prints '[above]' as a supplied word, JPS 1917 'upon', NJPS 'on'. The same fixed title stands at 1 Sam 4:4; 2 Sam 6:2; Ps 80:2; 99:1 and 2 Kgs 19:15 (MT checked), and the corpus already prints 'who is enthroned on the cherubim' at the stable 2 Sam 6:2 (2-samuel-woh overlay yoshev-hakkeruvim-enthroned-on-the-cherubim-2-samuel-6-2; central cherubim-ezek lists 2SA-WOH-6:2). One divine title keeps one English form; the 'above' of Exod 25:22 (mēʿal hakkappōreṯ mibbên šᵉnê hakkᵉrūḇîm, MT checked) is reported in commentary. At 37:24 yarkᵉṯê is the noun that 14:13 and 14:15 render 'the far reaches' (overlay helel-zaphon-elyon-taunt-isaiah-14); both passages are taunts over a king who boasts of going up (ʾeʿĕleh 14:13; ʿālîṯî 37:24), and NJPS 'the remotest parts' shows that the spatial sense is standard. At 37:36 the subject of wayyaškîmû is unexpressed; ASV and JPS 1917 supply 'men', and the line supplies 'people' under the house rule for generic human nouns (wave I-4 ruling 13), because a bare 'they' would read as the dead Assyrians of the same sentence (the 33:4 indefinite 'they' carries no such ambiguity). (2) Where a modern word replaces an archaic ASV one ('contempt' for 'contumely', 37:3; 'arrogance' for 'arrogancy', 37:29) the sense is unchanged. (3) Concordance with the stable chapters decides 37:24 ('cypresses', 14:8; 'fruitful field', 10:18; 29:17; 32:15), 37:27 ('dismayed and ashamed', 20:5), 37:31 ('survivors', 4:2; 10:20), 37:35 ('protect', 31:5) and 37:32 ('The zeal of YHWH of hosts will do this', 9:6). (4) šaʾănān receives two English words for two senses: 'quiet' of a dwelling at rest (32:18; 33:20) and 'arrogance' of a person at ease in pride (37:29; cf. Amos 6:1 'at ease', Ps 123:4 parallel to 'the proud', ASV checked); JPS 1917 'uproar' and NJPS 'tumult' are reported in commentary. (5) At the textual points (37:17 ʿênᵉḵā without yod; 37:18 'lands'; 37:20 without ʾĕlōhîm; 37:25 without zārîm; 37:27 šᵉḏēmāh) the line keeps MT with ASV and JPS 1917 under overlay mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah; NJPS adopts the Kings or 1QIsaᵃ reading at 37:18, 20 and 27 and says so in its notes. (6) At 37:12 'Eden' is the Aramean state of Amos 1:5 (bêṯ ʿeḏen) and Ezek 27:23, vocalized ʿeḏen against the garden's ʿēḏen (Gen 2:8, MT checked); the line keeps ASV and the identification stays in commentary. (7) At 37:36 the central malakh-yhwh-messenger entry already lists ISA-37:36 and 2KGS-19:35; Isaiah renders malʾāḵ 'messenger' at every other site (14:32; 18:2; 33:7; 37:9, 14), so the entry is kept against ASV/JPS 1917 'the angel' and NJPS 'an angel'. Sources: ASV via bible-api.com; JPS 1917 and NJPS (Tanakh: The Holy Scriptures, published by JPS, 1985; not the Gender-Sensitive Edition) via Sefaria API v3; MT of Isa 37 and 2 Kgs 19 (Tanach with Ta'amei Hamikra) via Sefaria API v3; all checked 2026-11-27; Amos 6:1 and Ps 123:4 ASV via bible-api.com, checked 2026-11-27; lexica, 1QIsaᵃ, NRSV, LXX and Assyriological identifications (Bit-Adini, Taharqa, Urartu) recalled, not verified.

rationaleAppend: Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:4 diḇrê raḇ-šāqēh 'the words of the Rabshakeh' and 37:8 wayyāšoḇ raḇ-šāqēh 'So the Rabshakeh returned', with the article as at the chapter 36 sites (wave ruling 7). NJPS prints 'the Rabshakeh' at both verses; ASV has 'Rabshakeh' and JPS 1917 'Rab-shakeh' without the article (checked 2026-11-27). 2 Kgs 19:4, 8 have the same Hebrew (MT, Sefaria, checked).

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:2 'Eliakim, who was over the house, and Shebna the scribe' — ʾăšer ʿal-habbayiṯ in the 22:15 wording, as at 36:3, 22 (chapter 36 Editor). ASV and JPS 1917 'who was over the household', NJPS 'who was in charge of the palace'; hassôp̄ēr 'the scribe' in ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS ('Shebna, the scribe') (checked 2026-11-27). 2 Kgs 19:2 has the same phrase (MT, Sefaria, checked).

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): the expected site is now governed. 37:9 tirhāqāh meleḵ-kûš 'Tirhakah king of Cush'; ASV and JPS 1917 'Tirhakah king of Ethiopia', NJPS 'King Tirhakah of Nubia' (checked 2026-11-27). 2 Kgs 19:9 has meleḵ-kûš as well (MT, Sefaria, checked). The 'Expected site' sentence of wohChoice is now fulfilled and may be dropped on merge (scope-only).

Wave I-6 (Isa 37). Orchestrator: add '37:30' to the qere list in wohChoice on merge (scope-only). At 37:30 the ketiv ואכול (infinitive absolute ʾāḵôl) has the qere wᵉʾiḵlû 'and eat', which is translated, as by ASV, JPS 1917 and NJPS; 2 Kgs 19:29 writes wᵉʾiḵlû without a ketiv/qere (MT, Sefaria, checked 2026-11-27). MT is kept, with the parallel text of 2 Kgs 19 and the versions reported in commentary, at 37:17 ʿênᵉḵā written without the yod of Kings' plural (read as a defective plural with ASV and JPS 1917; NJPS 'Your eye'); 37:18 kol-hāʾărāṣôṯ (Kings haggôyim; NJPS adopts 'nations' with the note 'So 2 Kings 19.17, and 13 mss. here'); 37:20 without ʾĕlōhîm (Kings; NJPS '[are God]', 'Supplied from 2 Kings 19.19'); 37:25 māyim without Kings' zārîm (1QIsaᵃ reported, not verified); 37:27 šᵉḏēmāh (Kings šᵉḏēp̄āh; NJPS 'blasted', 'So ms. 1QIsa; cf. 2 Kings 19.26'). NJPS notes checked on Sefaria, 2026-11-27.

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): capital 'God' at 37:4, 17 ʾĕlōhîm ḥay 'the living God' (no article in Hebrew; ASV, JPS 1917, NJPS 'the living God', checked 2026-11-27; the singular adjective ḥay, against ʾĕlōhîm ḥayyîm at Deut 5:23; 1 Sam 17:26; Jer 10:10, MT checked) and at 37:16 ʾattāh-hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm 'you are God' (articular, as 45:18 hûʾ hāʾĕlōhîm 'he is God'; ASV and JPS 1917 'the God'). Lower case for the gods of the nations (37:12 ʾĕlōhê haggôyim), for the burned images 'for they were no gods' (37:19) and for 'Nisroch his god' (37:38).
Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:4 YHWH ʾĕlōheḵā 'YHWH your God' (twice); 37:10 ʾĕlōheḵā 'your God' (in the Assyrian's message); 37:20 YHWH ʾĕlōhênû 'O YHWH our God'.
Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:16 YHWH ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'O YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel' and 37:21 YHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl 'YHWH, the God of Israel' (ASV, JPS 1917; checked 2026-11-27).

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:16 and 37:32. The parallel 2 Kgs 19:15 has no ṣᵉḇāʾôṯ, and at 2 Kgs 19:31 the word is a qere without ketiv (MT, Sefaria, checked 2026-11-27); the differences are reported in commentary.

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): kol mamlᵉḵôṯ hāʾāreṣ 'all the kingdoms of the earth' (37:16, 20) and the creation merism 'the skies and the earth' (37:16), the universal horizon of Hezekiah's prayer. Territorial ʾereṣ in the chapter ('his own land', 37:7; 'their land', 37:18; 'the land of Ararat', 37:38) stays 'land'.
Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:24 ḥērap̄tā ʾăḏōnāy 'you have defied the Lord' (ASV; JPS 1917 'the Lord'; NJPS 'my Lord', checked 2026-11-27); the same in 2 Kgs 19:23 (MT checked).

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:19 maʿăśēh yᵉḏê-ʾāḏām 'the work of human hands', generic ʾāḏām rendered by the adjective as at 31:3 ('the Egyptians are human'); ASV and JPS 1917 'men's hands', NJPS 'man's handwork' (checked 2026-11-27). The same house rule (wave I-4 ruling 13) gives the supplied subject 'people' at 37:36, recorded in lexical-cruxes-isaiah-37.

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): 37:7 hinnî nôṯēn bô rûaḥ 'I will put a spirit in him', lower case, the rûaḥ YHWH puts into the Assyrian king (ASV, JPS 1917 'a spirit'; NJPS 'I will delude him', note 'Lit. "put a spirit in"', checked 2026-11-27). The kind of rûaḥ is not specified and the line does not specify it (cf. rûaḥ šeqer, 1 Kgs 22:22, MT checked).

Wave I-6 (Isa 37): the Translator's descriptive title 'Isaiah 37 — Hezekiah's prayer, the taunt over Sennacherib, and the deliverance of Jerusalem' is kept; YHWH house style throughout; reported speech in quotation marks (37:3-4, 6-7, 10-13, 16-20, 21-35), with the inner speech of the taunt in single quotation marks (37:24-25).
